key_insight: CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after neutron irradiation, while mild light-assisted annealing provides only partial recovery.
engineering_relevance: Space-power designs using thin-film CdTe must account for radiation damage across the substrate, absorber, and contacts, as well as trade-offs during annealing.
method: Irradiated cells in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor for 10–150 min at nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n cm⁻².
Characterized devices after 18 months of storage and measured transmission through co-irradiated FTO-coated glass.
Evaluated post-irradiation annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.
evidence_signal: Glass transmittance at 500 nm fell from 80% to 50% after 60 min of irradiation; annealed cells reached their highest efficiency after 4 h, but longer annealing substantially degraded fill factor.
watch_item: Delayed characterization and unresolved defect mechanisms limit predictions of in-orbit degradation and optimal recovery protocols.
paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
